extracted.intended_audience: HRSA staff, state and local health agencies, health workforce planners, researchers, and other stakeholders involved in Maternity Care Target Area (MCTA) and HPSA designation
extracted.subtask_description: Final HRSA criteria and point scales for identifying Maternity Care Health Professional Target Areas (MCTAs), including definitions, data sources, and the numeric scoring tables used to compute a 0–25 composite MCTA score. Effective implementation begins August 15, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite MCTA score (0–25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The weighted scores from five scoring criteria will be summed to develop a composite MCTA score ranging from zero to 25, with 25 indicating the greatest need for maternity care health professionals in the MCTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of the five criteria is assigned a relative weight based on significance; weighted scores are summed to produce the composite. Higher composite scores indicate higher degree of need. Implementation date: August 15, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-to-Full-Time-Equivalent Maternity Care Health Professional Ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures the number of women of childbearing age in the service area compared to the number of maternity care health professionals in the service area. Women of childbearing age are defined as ages 15–44; maternity care health professionals are defined as Obstetricians-Gynecologists (OB-GYNs) and Certified Nurse Midwives (CNMs). A population-to-provider ratio of 1,500:1 is the minimum requirement for a population to be considered reasonably served by OB-GYNs and CNMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Population-to-provider ratio point values:
- Ratio ≥6,000:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Population (Pop) ≥500 => 6 points
- 6,000:1 > Ratio ≥5,000:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Pop ≥400 => 5 points
- 5,000:1 > Ratio ≥3,000:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Pop ≥300 => 4 points
- 3,000:1 > Ratio ≥2,000:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Pop ≥200 => 3 points
- 2,000:1 > Ratio ≥1,500:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Pop ≥100 => 2 points
- Ratio <1,500:1, or No CNMs or OB-GYNs and Pop <100 => 0 points
Use these table thresholds to assign points toward the composite MCTA score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of population with income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of women of childbearing age (15–44) living in the service area at or below 200% of the FPL will be used to score MCTAs, using poverty data from the United States Census Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- ≥50% => 5 points
- 50% > Percentage ≥45% => 4 points
- 45% > Percentage ≥40% => 3 points
- 40% > Percentage ≥35% => 2 points
- 35% > Percentage ≥30% => 1 point
- <30% => 0 points
Use Census Bureau data to compute the percentage for the service area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel time/distance to the nearest source of accessible care outside of the MCTA
rubrics_metrics.description: The nearest source of accessible care is defined as the nearest provider trained and licensed to provide the necessary care, as determined by the Esri StreetMap Premium road network. Travel time/distance is defined as the average time to travel by road (minutes) or the actual distance in road miles to the nearest source of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Time ≥90 min or Distance ≥90 miles => 6 points
- 90 min > Time ≥75 min or 90 miles > Distance ≥75 miles => 5 points
- 75 min > Time ≥60 min or 75 miles > Distance ≥60 miles => 4 points
- 60 min > Time ≥45 min or 60 miles > Distance ≥45 miles => 3 points
- 45 min > Time ≥30 min or 45 miles > Distance ≥30 miles => 2 points
- Time <30 min and Distance <30 miles => 0 points
Use Esri StreetMap Premium road network for travel-time/distance determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fertility rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Fertility rate is included to reflect increased need where birth rates are higher. Women of childbearing age (15–44) derived from the American Community Survey; births derived from the National Vital Statistics System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values based on percentiles among all U.S. counties:
- Fertility Rate ≥90th Percentile => 2 points
- 90th Percentile > Fertility Rate ≥50th Percentile => 1 point
- Fertility Rate <50th Percentile => 0 points
Data sources: American Community Survey (denominator) and National Vital Statistics System (births).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maternal health indicators (composite)
rubrics_metrics.description: A maternal health index containing six indicators associated with poor maternal health outcomes: pre-pregnancy obesity, pre-pregnancy diabetes, pre-pregnancy hypertension, cigarette smoking before or during pregnancy, prenatal care initiation in the first trimester (measured as prevalence of no prenatal care in first trimester), and a behavioral health access factor. Only women ages 15–44 are considered. Data sources: National Vital Statistics System Natality file for five indicators; Shortage Designation Management System Mental HPSA file for behavioral health access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sub-indicator has its own point rule (see sub-items). The maternal health indicators sub-scores are combined per the MCTA scoring rules to contribute to the composite MCTA score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-pregnancy obesity (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-pregnancy obesity is defined as having a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher. Scoring compares local prevalence to national county percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Prevalence of pre-pregnancy obesity ≥50th percentile among all counties => 1 point
- Prevalence <50th percentile => 0 points
Data source: National Vital Statistics System Natality file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-pregnancy diabetes (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-pregnancy diabetes prevalence compared to county percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Prevalence ≥50th percentile among all counties => 1 point
- Prevalence <50th percentile => 0 points
Data source: National Vital Statistics System Natality file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-pregnancy hypertension (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-pregnancy hypertension prevalence compared to county percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Prevalence ≥50th percentile among all counties => 1 point
- Prevalence <50th percentile => 0 points
Data source: National Vital Statistics System Natality file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cigarette smoking before or during pregnancy (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevalence of cigarette smoking before or during pregnancy among women in the area compared to county percentiles. Smoking before pregnancy is defined as smoking one or more cigarettes daily for the 3 months prior to pregnancy; smoking during pregnancy is defined as smoking one or more cigarettes during any trimester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Prevalence ≥50th percentile among all counties => 1 point
- Prevalence <50th percentile => 0 points
Data source: National Vital Statistics System Natality file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prenatal care initiation in the first trimester (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured as prevalence of women who did not initiate prenatal care in the first trimester (i.e., prevalence of no prenatal care in first trimester) compared to county percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point values:
- Prevalence of no prenatal care in first trimester ≥50th percentile among all counties => 1 point
- Prevalence <50th percentile => 0 points
Data source: National Vital Statistics System Natality file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral health factor (maternal health indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards a point if portion or all of the MCTA service area is designated as a Mental Health HPSA meeting specified population-to-provider median ratio thresholds based on mental health provider type; otherwise zero points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Point = 1 if portion or all of MCTA service area is designated as a Mental Health HPSA meeting the following population-to-provider ratio thresholds (median) based on its mental health provider type:
- Psychiatrist ONLY: Psychiatrist population-to-provider ratio ≥45,000:1
- Core Mental Health ONLY: Core mental health population-to-provider ratio ≥18,000:1
- Psychiatrist and Core Mental Health: Psychiatrist population-to-provider ratio ≥35,000:1 and Core mental health population-to-provider ratio ≥6,000:1
- No Psychiatrists or Core Mental Health Providers: ≥7,500: 0
If the Mental Health designation does not meet the thresholds above, or the area is not designated as a Mental Health HPSA, award 0 points.
Data source: Shortage Designation Management System Mental HPSA file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: women of childbearing age
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the MCTA criteria, 'women of childbearing age' is defined as women between the ages of 15–44 years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This age definition is used for population denominators in the population-to-provider ratio, poverty percentage, maternal health indicators, and fertility rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: maternity care health professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Maternity care health professionals for scoring purposes are defined as Obstetricians-Gynecologists (OB-GYNs) and Certified Nurse Midwives (CNMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines which provider counts are included in the population-to-provider ratio. HRSA may continue to evaluate components of this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and technical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice specifies data sources and technical tools used to calculate criteria and sub-scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key data sources/methods: United States Census Bureau poverty data; American Community Survey (women 15–44 denominator); National Vital Statistics System Natality file (births and maternal indicators); Shortage Designation Management System Mental HPSA file (behavioral health factor); Esri StreetMap Premium road network (travel time/distance). If methods fall under the Paperwork Reduction Act, HRSA will seek OMB clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) — removal from MCTA criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: HRSA proposed and is implementing removal of the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) as a criterion for MCTAs and reallocated its two points: one to population-to-provider ratio and one to travel time/distance to nearest accessible care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary of comments: 3 commenters supported removal (arguing reallocation better measures access and helps rural communities); 10 commenters opposed removal and recommended retaining SVI or replacing it with similar metrics (e.g., Social Deprivation Index) and recommended impact analyses. HRSA rationale: SVI is intended for emergency preparedness rather than measuring access to care; reallocation better aligns with congressional intent to quantify provider availability and distances to care. HRSA conducted an impact analysis (reported in the Feb 3, 2026 FRN) and anticipates an overall 6.6% increase to MCTA scores. HRSA may continue to evaluate components and definitions.
